blocks.text: This SOP establishes the framework followed by Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd to identify occupational health and safety risks, prevent workplace injuries and illnesses, protect employees and contract workers, and ensure compliance with applicable occupational health and safety requirements.

The procedure defines requirements for workplace risk assessment, chemical safety, personal protective equipment management, employee health monitoring, safety training, emergency preparedness, incident investigation, and safety performance monitoring.
This SOP applies to all employees, contract workers, trainees, visitors, and service personnel working within Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd premises.
The procedure covers:

API manufacturing operations
Production areas
Quality Control laboratories
Quality Assurance areas
Research and Development activities
Warehouse and material handling operations
Utility areas
Maintenance activities
Administrative offices

responsibilities: Coordinate implementation of this procedure.
Maintain required records and documentation.
Monitor compliance with the requirements of this SOP.
Implement health and safety programs and procedures.
Conduct risk assessments, inspections, and safety training.
Monitor workplace health and safety performance.
Ensure compliance with health and safety requirements within their areas of responsibility.
Support implementation of corrective and preventive actions.
Ensure employees receive required training and PPE.
Follow applicable health and safety procedures and instructions.
Use provided PPE and safety equipment correctly.
Report hazards, incidents, and unsafe conditions promptly.

steps.heading: Employee Safety Training and Competency Development

body.text: All employees receive safety training according to their job responsibilities.
Training is provided:

During joining induction.
Before assigning hazardous work.
During process changes.
Periodically through refresher training.
Safety training topics include:

Workplace safety rules
Chemical handling practices
PPE requirements
Fire prevention and firefighting
Emergency response procedures
Incident reporting
Safe work practices
Occupational health hazards
Training effectiveness may be evaluated through:

Knowledge assessments
Practical demonstrations
Supervisor observations

steps.heading: Workplace Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment

body.text: The EHS Department conducts hazard identification and risk assessments for workplace activities to identify potential occupational health and safety risks.
Risk assessments are performed for:

Chemical handling activities
Manufacturing processes
Laboratory operations
Equipment operation
Maintenance activities
Material handling
Storage operations
Emergency situations
The assessment evaluates:

Hazard identification
Potential impact on employees
Likelihood of occurrence
Existing control measures
Additional preventive actions required
Risk controls are implemented following the hierarchy of controls:

Elimination of hazard where possible
Substitution with safer alternatives
Engineering controls
Administrative controls
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Risk assessments are reviewed:

Annually
After process modification
After significant incidents
Before introduction of new chemicals or equipment

Records Maintained:

Employee Health & Safety Risk Assessment
Hazard Identification Register
Corrective Action Records
The EHS Department identifies PPE requirements based on workplace hazards and job activities.
PPE requirements may include:

Safety helmet
Safety shoes
Safety goggles
Chemical-resistant gloves
Protective clothing
Face shields
Respiratory protection equipment
The PPE management process includes:

Hazard-based PPE selection.
PPE issue to employees before starting assigned work.
Employee training on correct PPE usage.
Periodic inspection of PPE condition.
Replacement of damaged or ineffective PPE.
Supervisors verify PPE compliance during routine operations.
Due to API manufacturing activities, Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd implements controls for safe handling, storage, and use of chemicals.
Before handling chemicals:

Employees are trained on chemical hazards and safe handling requirements.
Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are made available for applicable chemicals.
Required PPE is identified based on chemical hazards.
Chemical handling controls include:

Proper chemical labeling and identification.
Storage according to compatibility requirements.
Use of designated chemical handling areas.
Availability of spill response materials.
Prevention of unauthorized access to chemical storage areas.
Employees handling hazardous chemicals shall follow approved operating procedures and emergency response requirements.

Records Maintained:

Chemical Inventory Records
SDS Records
For high-risk activities, Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd follows a Permit-to-Work system.
Activities requiring permits may include:

Hot work
Confined space entry
Electrical work
Work at height
Maintenance activities involving hazardous energy
Before work begins:

Hazards are assessed.
Required precautions are identified.
Authorized persons approve the permit.
Work area safety conditions are verified.

Records Maintained:

Permit-to-Work Records
Work Authorization Documents
The EHS Department conducts routine workplace inspections to verify implementation of safety requirements.
Inspections cover:

PPE usage
Housekeeping standards
Chemical storage conditions
Emergency equipment availability
Safety signage
Equipment safety conditions
Access routes and exits
Inspection findings are documented and corrective actions are assigned with responsible persons and completion timelines.

Records Maintained:

Safety Inspection Checklist
Corrective Action Tracker
All workplace incidents, accidents, and near misses shall be reported immediately to the supervisor and EHS Department.
Incident management includes:

Immediate response and injured employee support.
Incident reporting and documentation.
Investigation to identify root causes.
Implementation of corrective and preventive actions.
Verification of action effectiveness.
Lessons learned are communicated to relevant employees to prevent recurrence.
Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd implements employee health monitoring based on workplace exposure risks and job requirements.
Health monitoring includes:
Pre-Employment Medical Examination
Before joining, employees undergo medical evaluation where required to confirm fitness for assigned work.
Periodic Health Check-up
Employees exposed to occupational hazards undergo periodic medical examinations as per applicable requirements.
Health monitoring may include:

General health assessment
Vision examination
Respiratory health assessment
Exposure-related medical checks
Medical information is maintained confidentially and accessed only by authorized personnel.

Records Maintained:

Medical Examination Records
Health Monitoring Reports
The EHS Department monitors safety performance through:

Incident frequency
Near-miss reporting
Safety inspection findings
Training completion
Corrective action closure status
Safety performance is reviewed periodically with management to identify improvement opportunities.

blocks.text: The purpose of this procedure is to establish controls for protecting the health, safety, and well-being of non-employees who enter, work at, or visit Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd facilities. This procedure ensures that contractors, visitors, consultants, service providers, transport personnel, auditors, customers, and other third parties are informed of applicable health and safety requirements and perform their activities in a safe and controlled manner.

responsibilities: Coordinate implementation of this procedure.
Provide health and safety guidance to non-employees.
Monitor compliance with applicable health and safety requirements.
Ensure non-employees working within their departments comply with applicable safety requirements.
Coordinate with EHS for high-risk activities and permit approvals.
Control site access and maintain visitor entry records.
Ensure completion of visitor registration and entry requirements.
Follow applicable site safety requirements.
Use required personal protective equipment.
Report hazards, incidents, and unsafe conditions immediately.

body.text: 3.3.1 Pre-Entry Requirements

Contractor Qualification Review

Contractors performing work on company premises shall be evaluated before engagement to ensure they possess the necessary competency, licenses, certifications, manpower capability, and safety arrangements required for the assigned work.

Document Verification

Relevant documents such as employee identification records, training certificates, insurance documents, statutory registrations, and work-related certifications shall be reviewed before granting work authorization where applicable.

Work Scope Review

The concerned department shall communicate the scope of work, location of work, expected duration, and applicable safety requirements before commencement of activities.

Visitor Registration

All visitors shall register at the security gate before entering company premises and provide relevant identification and visit details.

Host Authorization

Visitors shall enter operational areas only after approval from the concerned department or designated host employee.

Visitor Identification

Visitor badges or temporary access permits shall be issued and displayed throughout the visit.

Restricted Access

Access to production areas, laboratories, chemical storage locations, utility areas, and other restricted locations shall only be permitted when authorized and accompanied by designated personnel.

Site Safety Orientation

Contractors and long-term service providers shall receive site-specific safety induction before commencing work activities.

Visitor Safety Briefing

Visitors entering operational areas shall receive a brief safety orientation covering emergency exits, assembly points, restricted areas, emergency contact information, and required precautions.

Communication of Hazards

Relevant workplace hazards, emergency procedures, and applicable safety rules shall be communicated before access is granted.

Mandatory PPE Compliance

Non-employees entering operational areas shall wear PPE appropriate to the hazards present within the work area.

Area-Specific PPE Requirements

Depending on the work location and activity, required PPE may include safety shoes, helmets, safety goggles, gloves, high-visibility vests, hearing protection, respiratory protection, or other protective equipment.

PPE Monitoring

Supervisors and EHS personnel shall monitor compliance with PPE requirements and may restrict access where PPE requirements are not met.

Work Planning

Contractors shall perform work only within the approved scope and designated work area.

Compliance with Site Rules

Contractors shall comply with all applicable company procedures, safety instructions, signage, and operational controls while performing work on company premises.

Supervision and Monitoring

Contractor activities shall be monitored periodically by the concerned department and EHS personnel to verify compliance with health and safety requirements.

Subcontractor Control

Contractors engaging subcontractors shall ensure that subcontractor personnel comply with the same health and safety requirements applicable to contractor personnel.

High-Risk Activities

A Permit-to-Work shall be obtained before commencing high-risk activities including:

Hot work
Work at height
Confined space entry
Electrical maintenance
Excavation work
Line breaking or chemical system maintenance

Permit Verification

The concerned department and EHS representative shall verify implementation of required safety precautions before permit approval.

Permit Closure

Upon completion of work, the work area shall be inspected and the permit formally closed by the authorized person.

Vehicle Movement

Drivers and transport personnel shall comply with site traffic rules, designated speed limits, parking requirements, and loading/unloading instructions.

Restricted Activities

Smoking, alcohol consumption, unauthorized photography, tampering with equipment, horseplay, and unauthorized access to operational systems are prohibited.

Housekeeping Requirements

Contractors shall maintain good housekeeping standards and ensure work areas are kept free from unnecessary waste, obstructions, and hazards.

Immediate Reporting

Any accident, injury, near miss, unsafe act, unsafe condition, environmental incident, or property damage involving non-employees shall be reported immediately.

Incident Investigation

Relevant incidents involving non-employees shall be investigated to identify root causes and determine corrective and preventive actions.

Corrective Action Implementation

Identified corrective actions shall be assigned, tracked, and verified for completion.

narrative.text:
Safety Inspections

EHS personnel may conduct periodic inspections of contractor activities and work areas to verify compliance with company safety requirements.

Non-Compliance Management

Repeated safety violations, failure to comply with permit requirements, refusal to use PPE, or unsafe work practices may result in suspension of work, removal from site, or termination of contractor access privileges.

Performance Review

Contractor safety performance may be considered during contractor evaluation, renewal, and future engagement decisions.

blocks.text:
This procedure establishes a structured process for evaluating employee performance at Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

The objective is to:

Assess employee performance against defined expectations.
Recognize achievements and contributions.
Identify competency and development needs.
Support career development, succession planning, promotions, and performance improvement.
Align individual performance with organizational objectives.

This procedure applies to all permanent employees who have successfully completed their probation period.

The process covers:

Annual performance evaluations.
Mid-year performance discussions.
Individual Career Development Plans (ICDPs).
Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs).
Promotion and succession planning inputs.
Training and development planning.

responsibilities: Coordinate evaluation process, maintain records, ensure consistency, monitor development plans, maintain confidentiality
Set objectives, monitor performance, conduct evaluations, provide feedback, identify development needs
Review evaluation outcomes, ensure fairness, support development and succession planning
Complete self-evaluation, participate in discussions, implement agreed development actions

rows: Coordinate evaluation process, maintain records, ensure consistency, monitor development plans, maintain confidentiality
Set objectives, monitor performance, conduct evaluations, provide feedback, identify development needs
Review evaluation outcomes, ensure fairness, support development and succession planning
Complete self-evaluation, participate in discussions, implement agreed development actions

body.text: At the beginning of the review cycle, Reporting Managers shall establish employee objectives based on:

Job responsibilities.
Department targets.
Quality and compliance requirements.
Productivity expectations.
Improvement initiatives.
Behavioral expectations.
Objectives shall be discussed with employees and documented.
Employee performance shall be monitored throughout the year using:

KPI achievement.
Work quality and productivity.
Training completion.
Attendance and punctuality.
Compliance records.
Audit observations.
Project completion.
Workplace behavior.
Managers shall provide regular feedback and guidance during the review period.
A mid-year review shall be conducted to discuss:

Progress against objectives.
Achievements.
Challenges.
Development requirements.
Required management support.
Performance concerns identified during this stage shall be documented with improvement actions.
Before annual evaluation, employees shall complete a self-assessment covering:

Key achievements.
Completed responsibilities.
Improvement initiatives.
Training completed.
Challenges faced.
Development needs.
Career aspirations.

The Reporting Manager shall evaluate employee performance based on documented evidence.

Assessment shall consider:
Role Effectiveness

Achievement of objectives.
Quality and accuracy of work.
Technical knowledge.
Compliance with SOPs and company requirements.
Problem-solving ability.
Accountability.
Communication and Workplace Behavior

Professional conduct.
Communication skills.
Team interaction.
Cooperation with stakeholders.
Productivity and Growth

Learning ability.
Initiative and improvement efforts.
Adaptability.
Participation in training.
Team Contribution

Support to team members.
Cross-functional collaboration.
Participation in projects and improvement activities.
Employees shall be evaluated using the following rating scale:
Rating controls:

Ratings shall be supported by performance evidence.
Ratings of 5 and 1 require documented justification.
Department Heads shall review ratings before final approval.
HR shall verify evaluation consistency.
The Reporting Manager shall conduct a review discussion with the employee covering:

Evaluation results.
Strengths and achievements.
Improvement areas.
Training requirements.
Career goals.
Future expectations.
Employees may provide comments or feedback regarding the evaluation outcome.
Approved evaluation records shall be maintained by HR.

Based on evaluation outcomes, employees may be provided with an Individual Career Development Plan to support competency development and career growth.

The ICDP shall include:

Career goals.
Current strengths.
Development gaps.
Required actions.
Training requirements.
Target timelines.
Success indicators.
Development activities may include:

Technical training.
Certifications.
Coaching and mentoring.
Job rotation.
Cross-functional assignments.
Leadership development.
ICDP progress shall be reviewed periodically by the Reporting Manager.
A Performance Improvement Plan shall be initiated when:

Employee receives rating of 1 or 2.
Significant performance gaps are identified.
Repeated concerns remain unresolved.
Quality, compliance, or productivity issues occur.
The PIP shall define:

Performance gaps.
Expected improvement standards.
Required actions.
Training/coaching support.
Review timelines.

PIP Duration: Normally 60–90 days.

Progress shall be reviewed monthly and documented.
Performance evaluation results shall support decisions related to:

Promotions.
Career progression.
Increased responsibilities.
Succession planning.
Leadership development.
Decisions shall consider:

Performance results.
Competency level.
Experience.
behavioral performance.
Business requirements.

Employees who disagree with evaluation results may submit an appeal to HR within 10 working days of receiving the evaluation.

HR shall review the concern with the Reporting Manager and Department Head and communicate the final decision within 15 working days.

blocks.text:
The purpose of this procedure is to establish a structured and objective process for evaluating the performance of Buyers at Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd. The evaluation process enables the organization to assess employee contributions, procurement effectiveness, supplier management performance, communication skills, sustainability engagement, and overall achievement of departmental objectives.

The evaluation results are used to support employee development, performance improvement, succession planning, career progression, and workforce capability enhancement.

This procedure applies to all employees performing Buyer, Procurement Executive, Senior Buyer, and similar procurement-related roles responsible for supplier sourcing, procurement coordination, purchase order management, supplier performance monitoring, and procurement support activities.

The procedure covers annual performance evaluations, development planning, performance improvement actions, and evaluation record management.

responsibilities: Coordinate evaluation activities, maintain records, and monitor completion of evaluations.
Conduct evaluations, assign ratings, provide feedback, and recommend development actions.
Review and approve evaluation outcomes and development recommendations.
Complete self-assessment and participate in evaluation discussions.

substeps.text: Human Resources shall initiate the annual performance evaluation process during April of each year.
The evaluation period shall normally cover employee performance during the previous financial year.
Employees who have completed a minimum of six months of service during the review period shall be eligible for evaluation.
HR shall communicate evaluation timelines and distribute performance evaluation forms to eligible employees and reporting managers.

body.text: Employees shall complete the self-assessment section of the Buyer Performance Evaluation Form.

The self-assessment shall provide an overview of performance achievements, challenges encountered, improvement initiatives undertaken, training programmes completed, and contributions made during the review period.
Employees shall provide supporting examples wherever applicable.
Completed self-assessments shall be submitted to the Reporting Manager within the specified timeline.
The Reporting Manager shall assess the employee's contribution towards supplier sustainability management and responsible procurement practices.
Assessment shall consider:

Follow-up of supplier sustainability questionnaires and declarations.
Collection and maintenance of supplier sustainability information.
Communication of customer sustainability requirements to suppliers.
Participation in supplier sustainability assessments and reviews.
Support provided to suppliers for corrective actions related to sustainability requirements.
Contribution towards increasing supplier sustainability awareness.
Supporting evidence may include supplier assessment records, supplier communication records, sustainability tracking reports, and supplier improvement activities.
The Reporting Manager shall assess the employee's ability to communicate effectively with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
Assessment shall consider:

Timeliness of responses to procurement-related requests.
Accuracy and professionalism of supplier communications.
Communication of procurement status updates to relevant departments.
Timely escalation of procurement risks and supply disruptions.
Ability to resolve supplier-related and internal coordination issues.
Collaboration with Production, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Finance, and other departments.
Internal stakeholder feedback may be considered during the evaluation process.

steps.heading: 5.4.5 Evaluation of Individual Performance and Work Effectiveness

body.text: The Reporting Manager shall evaluate the employee's effectiveness in carrying out assigned procurement responsibilities.
Assessment shall consider:

Timely conversion of approved Purchase Requisitions into Purchase Orders.
Monitoring and follow-up of open Purchase Orders.
Procurement documentation accuracy.
Timely completion of assigned procurement activities.
Compliance with procurement procedures and approval requirements.
Ability to manage urgent procurement requirements.
Contribution towards uninterrupted availability of materials and services.
Initiative shown in resolving procurement-related challenges.
Procurement records, purchase order reports, procurement trackers, and operational feedback may be reviewed as part of the evaluation.

steps.heading: 5.4.6 Evaluation of Supplier Engagement and Performance Management

body.text: The Reporting Manager shall evaluate the employee's ability to manage supplier relationships and supplier performance.
Assessment shall consider:

Follow-up of supplier delivery commitments.
Resolution of supplier-related issues.
Supplier responsiveness and communication effectiveness.
Monitoring of supplier delivery performance.
Participation in supplier evaluation and qualification activities.
Identification of alternate suppliers where required.
Coordination with suppliers during material shortages, delivery delays, or operational disruptions.
Contribution towards maintaining continuity of supply.
Supplier performance reports and supplier evaluation records may be reviewed during assessment.
The Reporting Manager shall assign ratings against each evaluation category based on available evidence and observed performance.
Evaluation comments shall include:

Key strengths.
Significant achievements.
Areas requiring improvement.
Recommended development actions.
Completed evaluations shall be submitted to the Department Head for review and approval.
Upon completion of the evaluation, the Reporting Manager shall conduct a formal performance review meeting with the employee.
The meeting shall include:

Discussion of evaluation results.
Review of procurement achievements.
Discussion of performance challenges.
Identification of development opportunities.
Discussion of future performance expectations.
Employees shall be given an opportunity to provide feedback and comments regarding their evaluation.

Rating Guidelines

Outstanding: Performance consistently exceeds all expectations and demonstrates exceptional contribution.

Exceeds Expectations: Performance regularly exceeds established requirements.
Meets Expectations: Performance consistently meets job requirements.
Needs Improvement: Performance does not consistently meet expectations and requires improvement.
Unsatisfactory: Significant performance deficiencies requiring immediate corrective action.

blocks.text: An Individual Development Plan shall be prepared where development opportunities or competency gaps are identified.
Development plans may focus on:

Sustainable procurement practices.
Supplier management skills.
Negotiation and commercial management.
Procurement analytics and reporting.
Communication and stakeholder management.

Leadership development.

Each development plan shall define development objectives, planned actions, responsible persons, target completion dates, and success indicators.
Progress shall be reviewed periodically by the Reporting Manager.
Employees receiving a rating of "Needs Improvement" or "Unsatisfactory" may be placed under a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP).
Improvement plans shall include:

Identified performance gaps.
Expected performance standards.
Corrective actions.
Required training and support.
Review milestones.
Target completion dates.
Progress shall be monitored by the Reporting Manager and Human Resources Department.
The following records shall be maintained:

Buyer Performance Evaluation Forms.
Individual Development Plans.
Performance Improvement Plans.
Training Records.
Procurement Performance Reports.

sops.title: Employee Career Progression and Advancement Procedure

blocks.text: The purpose of this procedure is to establish a fair, transparent, and merit-based process for employee promotion and career advancement at Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd. The procedure aims to ensure that all employees are provided equal access to career growth opportunities based on performance, competencies, experience, potential, and business requirements without discrimination.
This procedure applies to all permanent employees of Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd across all departments and functions.
The procedure covers:

Employee promotions.
Internal career advancement opportunities.
Internal job transfers.
Succession planning recommendations.
Equal opportunity requirements.
Promotion approval process.

responsibilities: Coordinate promotion reviews, maintain records, and ensure compliance with equal opportunity principles.
Evaluate employee performance and recommend eligible employees for promotion.
Review promotion recommendations and assess business requirements.
Approve promotions for managerial and critical positions.
Participate in performance reviews and development activities.

body.text:
Promotion opportunities may arise due to organizational growth, business expansion, workforce restructuring, succession planning requirements, creation of new positions, or employee vacancies.
Department Heads shall review workforce requirements annually and identify positions that may require internal advancement.
Human Resources shall maintain records of available advancement opportunities and communicate them to relevant departments.
Internal candidates shall be considered before external recruitment is initiated wherever feasible.
Employees may be considered for promotion based on the following criteria:

Consistent achievement of performance objectives during annual performance evaluations.
Demonstration of technical competence required for the higher position.
Compliance with company policies, procedures, and workplace standards.
Positive disciplinary record during the review period.
Demonstrated leadership potential and ability to handle additional responsibilities.
Completion of mandatory training programmes applicable to the target role.
Ability to perform responsibilities associated with the proposed position.
Promotion eligibility does not guarantee promotion and shall remain subject to business requirements and position availability.
Reporting Managers shall evaluate employees using available performance evaluation records.
Assessment shall consider:

Performance ratings achieved during previous review cycles.
Quality and accuracy of work performed.
Productivity and achievement of departmental objectives.
Problem-solving capabilities.
Initiative and innovation demonstrated.
Ability to work independently and within teams.
Leadership and supervisory capabilities where applicable.
Professional conduct and workplace behavior.
Employees consistently receiving performance ratings below expectations shall not normally be considered for promotion until performance improvement is demonstrated.
In addition to performance evaluation results, employees shall be assessed against the competency requirements of the proposed position.
Assessment may include:

Technical knowledge.
Functional expertise.
Communication skills.
Decision-making ability.
Leadership capability.
Stakeholder management skills.
Planning and organizational skills.
Regulatory and compliance awareness.
Additional interviews, assessments, or competency reviews may be conducted where required.

Vacant positions may be communicated internally through notice boards, emails, internal communication systems, or departmental announcements.
Employees meeting minimum qualification and experience requirements may apply for internal advancement opportunities.
Internal applicants shall be evaluated using the same objective criteria applied to promotion assessments.
Selection decisions shall be based on competency, performance, experience, and suitability for the role.
Internal transfers may be considered to support employee development and organizational requirements.

Promotion and career advancement decisions shall be based solely on merit, qualifications, performance, competency, experience, and business requirements.
Discrimination based on gender, age, religion, caste, ethnicity, nationality, disability, marital status, pregnancy, political opinion, union membership, or any other legally protected characteristic is strictly prohibited.
All employees shall be provided equal access to promotion opportunities and professional development programmes.
Reasonable accommodations shall be considered where required to ensure equal participation in promotion processes.
Human Resources shall review promotion recommendations to ensure compliance with equal opportunity principles.
Employees identified as high-potential candidates may be included in development programmes designed to prepare them for future responsibilities.
Development activities may include:

Technical training programmes.
Leadership development programmes.
Cross-functional assignments.
Mentoring and coaching.
Professional certification programmes.
Project leadership opportunities.
Individual Development Plans (IDPs) may be prepared to support career progression and succession planning activities.
Promotion recommendations shall be submitted by the Reporting Manager to the Department Head.
The Department Head shall review:

Employee performance history.
Competency assessment results.
Business requirements.
Position availability.
Budget considerations.
Human Resources shall review promotion recommendations for compliance with company policies and equal opportunity requirements.
Final approval shall be obtained from Senior Management for managerial and critical positions.
Approved promotions shall be formally communicated through a Promotion Letter issued by Human Resources.
The Promotion Letter shall specify:

New designation.
Effective date.
Revised reporting structure.
Compensation revisions where applicable.
Key responsibilities associated with the new role.
Promotion records shall be maintained within the employee personnel file.

narrative.text: Human Resources shall periodically review promotion trends and career advancement data.
Reviews may include:

Internal promotion rates.
Department-wise promotion statistics.
Gender diversity in promotions.
Development programmes participation.
Succession planning readiness.
Identified gaps shall be reviewed and improvement actions implemented where necessary.

sops.title: Energy Efficiency and Low-Carbon Energy Management Procedure

blocks.text:
This procedure establishes the framework for improving energy efficiency, optimizing energy consumption, increasing the use of renewable energy, and reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with operations at Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

The procedure aims to support responsible energy management through the identification and implementation of energy conservation measures, low-carbon technologies, fuel-switching initiatives, renewable energy projects, waste heat recovery systems, and continuous improvement activities.

This procedure applies to all operational activities, utilities, buildings, infrastructure, equipment, and processes that consume energy at Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

The procedure covers:

Electricity consumption.
Fuel consumption.
Utility operations.
Process energy use.
Renewable energy projects.
Energy-efficient equipment and technology upgrades.
Waste heat recovery initiatives.
Low-carbon energy transition projects.

responsibilities: Approve energy efficiency objectives and initiatives.
Provide resources for implementation of energy improvement projects.
Review energy performance and progress periodically.
Monitor energy consumption.
Identify energy-saving opportunities.
Evaluate equipment efficiency.
Implement approved energy efficiency projects.
Maintain energy-related records.
Track energy performance indicators.
Monitor renewable energy and carbon reduction initiatives.
Support awareness and training activities.
Maintain energy performance reports.
Support implementation of energy conservation initiatives.
Promote responsible energy use within their departments.
Follow energy conservation practices.
Report energy wastage, leaks, or inefficient equipment operation.

body.text:
The Company shall monitor energy consumption across operations to identify opportunities for improving energy efficiency and reducing energy-related greenhouse gas emissions.

Energy consumption data may be collected from:

Electricity bills.
Fuel consumption records.
Utility meter readings.
Equipment operating records.
Renewable energy generation records.
Energy performance shall be reviewed periodically to identify significant energy-consuming activities and opportunities for improvement.

The Company shall implement energy efficiency measures aimed at reducing overall energy consumption and improving operational performance.

Such measures may include:

Installation of LED lighting systems.
Replacement of inefficient motors and pumps with energy-efficient models.
Installation of Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs).
Optimization of HVAC systems.
Optimization of compressed air systems.
Process automation and control improvements.
Preventive maintenance programs to maintain equipment efficiency.
Energy-efficient utility and facility upgrades.
Energy-saving opportunities identified through operational reviews, inspections, audits, or employee suggestions shall be evaluated for implementation.

steps.heading: Fuel Switching and Low-Carbon Energy Transition

body.text:
The Company shall evaluate opportunities to transition from higher-carbon energy sources to cleaner and lower-emission alternatives where technically and economically feasible.

Initiatives may include:

Replacement of diesel-powered equipment with electric alternatives.
Transition from conventional fuels to lower-carbon fuels.
Electrification of operational processes and utility systems.
Adoption of cleaner energy technologies.
Reduction of dependence on carbon-intensive fuels.
Fuel-switching projects shall be prioritized based on potential energy efficiency improvements and greenhouse gas emission reduction benefits.

steps.heading: Waste Heat Recovery and Energy Recovery Systems

body.text:
The Company shall assess opportunities to recover and utilize waste energy generated during operations to improve overall energy efficiency.

Potential initiatives may include:

Installation of waste heat recovery systems.
Recovery and reuse of process heat.
Heat exchangers and energy recovery units.
Combined Heat and Power (CHP) systems.
Cogeneration systems.
Reuse of recovered energy within operational processes.
Where technically feasible, recovered energy shall be utilized to reduce overall energy demand and improve operational efficiency.

The Company shall promote the use of renewable energy to reduce dependence on conventional energy sources and lower operational carbon emissions.

Renewable energy initiatives may include:

Installation of rooftop solar photovoltaic systems.
Solar water heating systems.
Procurement of renewable electricity from approved suppliers.
Renewable energy power purchase agreements.
Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs), where applicable.
Evaluation of additional renewable energy opportunities suitable for operations.
Progress in renewable energy adoption shall be monitored periodically.

steps.heading: Energy Considerations in Equipment and Technology Upgrades

body.text:
Energy performance shall be considered when purchasing new equipment, replacing existing assets, or implementing technology upgrades.

Selection criteria may include:

Energy efficiency performance.
Expected energy savings.
Equipment operating efficiency.
Life-cycle energy consumption.
Potential reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.
Reliability and maintenance requirements.

Preference shall be given to technologies that contribute to long-term energy efficiency improvements and support the Company's sustainability objectives.

Examples may include:

High-efficiency motors.
Energy-efficient chillers.
Efficient boilers.
Smart energy monitoring systems.
Automated process control systems.
Advanced utility management technologies.

The Company shall promote employee participation in energy conservation initiatives.

Awareness activities may include:

Energy conservation training.
Awareness campaigns.
Energy-saving communications.
Employee suggestion programs.
Employees are encouraged to identify and report opportunities for reducing energy consumption and improving operational efficiency.
Energy performance shall be reviewed periodically using indicators such as:

Total energy consumption.
Electricity consumption.
Fuel consumption.
Renewable energy consumption.
Percentage of renewable energy usage.
Energy intensity.
Energy savings achieved through implemented projects.
Carbon emission intensity.
Improvement opportunities identified during reviews shall be incorporated into future action plans and operational objectives.

narrative.text: The effectiveness of this procedure may be monitored using indicators such as:

Total energy consumption.
Energy intensity per unit of production.
Renewable energy generation or procurement.
Percentage renewable energy contribution.
Number of energy efficiency projects implemented.
Fuel consumption reduction.
Carbon emission intensity reduction.
Results shall be reviewed periodically by relevant departments and Senior Management.

blocks.text: The following records shall be maintained, as applicable:

Electricity consumption records.
Fuel consumption records.
Utility meter readings.
Energy monitoring reports.
Energy audit reports.
Renewable energy records.
Energy efficiency project records.
Equipment upgrade records.
Training and awareness records.
Energy performance review records.

sops.title: ESG Risk Screening and Third-Party Management Procedure

blocks.text: The purpose of this procedure is to establish a structured approach for conducting Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) due diligence on suppliers, contractors, service providers, consultants, distributors, logistics partners, and other third parties engaged by Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

This procedure aims to identify, assess, manage, and monitor ESG-related risks within the supply chain and business relationships while promoting responsible sourcing, ethical business conduct, labour rights, environmental stewardship, and regulatory compliance.

This procedure applies to all new and existing third parties that provide goods, services, raw materials, transportation, contract labour, consultancy services, waste management services, facility management services, and other business-related activities for Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.
The procedure covers:

Supplier onboarding.
Supplier qualification.
Vendor approval.
Contractor engagement.
Third-party ESG risk assessment.
Ongoing supplier monitoring.
Corrective action management.
Supplier re-evaluation.

responsibilities: Ensure implementation of ESG due diligence requirements during supplier selection and evaluation.
Conduct ESG assessments and monitor supplier ESG performance.
Support supplier evaluations relevant to their operational areas.
Verify compliance with applicable quality and regulatory requirements.
Provide requested ESG information and cooperate during assessments.
Review high-risk findings and approve risk mitigation actions where required.

body.text: Prior to onboarding a new supplier or contractor, the Procurement Department shall collect basic supplier information including:

Company name and registration details.
Business address and contact information.
Nature of products or services supplied.
Key management contacts.
Regulatory licenses and certifications.
GST and statutory registration details.
Suppliers shall be registered in the Approved Vendor List (AVL) only after completion of the applicable assessment process.
All new suppliers and third parties shall undergo an initial ESG screening before approval.
The screening shall evaluate potential risks associated with:
Environmental Factors

Environmental permits and regulatory compliance.
Waste management practices.
Hazardous material handling.
Pollution prevention measures.
Energy and water management practices.
Social Factors

Child labour practices.
Forced labour risks.
Working conditions.
Occupational health and safety management.
Employee welfare practices.
Working hours and wage compliance.
Governance Factors

Business ethics practices.
Anti-bribery and anti-corruption controls.
Regulatory compliance history.
Data protection and confidentiality practices.
Conflict of interest concerns.
Based on the screening results, suppliers shall be classified into the following risk categories:

rows: Limited ESG risks identified and adequate controls demonstrated.
Some ESG risks identified requiring monitoring or corrective actions.
Significant ESG concerns identified requiring management review and mitigation actions.

body.text: Risk Considerations
Risk categorization may consider:

Type of goods or services supplied.
Geographic location.
Labour-intensive operations.
Environmental impact of operations.
Previous compliance violations.
Regulatory enforcement history.
Reputational risks.
Depending on the risk level, suppliers may be requested to provide supporting documentation including:

Business registration certificates.
Environmental permits and licenses.
ISO certifications.
Occupational Health & Safety certifications.
Sustainability policies.
Labour and Human Rights policies.
Business Ethics policies.
Anti-Corruption policies.
Environmental management procedures.
Worker welfare programmes.
ESG assessment questionnaires.
Corrective action records.
The ESG Coordinator shall review submitted information and document findings.
Medium and High-Risk suppliers may be required to complete an ESG Self-Assessment Questionnaire.
Assessment areas may include:

Environmental management.
Energy and water conservation.
Waste management.
Occupational health and safety.
Labour practices.
Human rights protection.
Ethics and compliance.
Business continuity measures.
Responses shall be reviewed and evaluated by the Sustainability Coordinator and Procurement Department.
The supplier approval decision shall be based on:

Business requirements.
Technical capability.
Quality performance.
ESG assessment results.
Regulatory compliance status.
Risk assessment outcome.
Approval decisions may be categorized as:

rows: Supplier meets business and ESG requirements.
Supplier approved subject to completion of corrective actions.
Significant ESG or compliance concerns identified.

body.text: Where ESG gaps are identified, suppliers may be requested to implement corrective actions.
Corrective actions may relate to:

Health and safety deficiencies.
Environmental non-compliance.
Labour rights concerns.
Missing policies or procedures.
Regulatory compliance issues.
Suppliers shall provide evidence of corrective action completion within the agreed timeline.
Procurement and Sustainability teams shall verify closure of corrective actions.
Approved suppliers shall be monitored periodically to ensure continued compliance.
Supplier performance reviews may consider:

Delivery performance.
Quality performance.
ESG performance.
Regulatory compliance status.
Corrective action closure.
High-Risk suppliers shall be reviewed annually.
Medium-Risk suppliers shall be reviewed every two years.
Low-Risk suppliers shall be reviewed every three years or when significant changes occur.

rows: Child Labour, Forced Labour or Serious Human Rights Violation

sops.title: Climate-Related Risk and Operational Resilience Procedure

blocks.text: This procedure establishes a systematic framework for identifying, assessing, mitigating, and monitoring climate-related risks, physical hazards, and business disruption risks that may affect employees, facilities, utilities, information systems, supply chain operations, product delivery, and business continuity at Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

The objective is to improve organizational resilience, minimize operational disruptions, protect employees and assets, maintain regulatory compliance, and ensure continuity of critical business activities during emergencies and unforeseen events.
This procedure applies to:

Manufacturing operations.
Utility and engineering systems.
Warehouse and storage facilities.
Administrative offices.
Information technology infrastructure.
Logistics and transportation activities.
Contractors and service providers operating at company premises.
The procedure covers climate-related hazards, physical hazards, utility failures, infrastructure disruptions, supply chain interruptions, and emergency recovery activities.

responsibilities: Approve climate resilience and business continuity strategies.
Allocate resources for risk mitigation initiatives.
Review significant climate and business continuity risks annually.
Conduct climate and physical hazard assessments.
Maintain the Climate Risk Register.
Coordinate emergency preparedness activities.
Monitor implementation of mitigation measures.
Maintain critical utilities and infrastructure.
Implement engineering controls for identified risks.
Maintain backup power and utility systems.
Maintain data backup and recovery systems.
Ensure continuity of critical IT infrastructure.
Assess supply chain vulnerabilities.
Identify alternate suppliers for critical materials.
Identify department-specific continuity requirements.
Support implementation of risk mitigation measures.
Follow emergency procedures.
Participate in emergency drills.
Report hazards and emergency situations immediately.

body.text: The EHS Department shall conduct a Climate Risk and Physical Hazard Assessment annually and whenever significant changes occur to operations, facilities, or infrastructure.
The assessment shall evaluate the following hazards:

rows: Heat stress, reduced productivity, increased cooling demand
Site access restrictions, water ingress, logistics delays
Damage to equipment, inventory loss, operational disruption
Reduced water availability for manufacturing and domestic use
Structural damage, power outages, transportation disruption
Loss of business-critical information and operational disruption

body.text: Each identified risk shall be evaluated based on likelihood, severity, and business impact.
Where workplace temperatures exceed safe operating conditions:

Drinking water stations shall be available in operational areas.
Ventilation and cooling systems shall be maintained.
Heat-generating equipment shall be monitored.
Employees exposed to high-temperature environments shall receive heat stress awareness training.
Prior to the monsoon season:

Drainage systems shall be inspected and cleaned.
Roofs and rainwater channels shall be inspected.
Flood-prone areas shall be identified and monitored.
Critical equipment and inventory shall be protected from potential water damage.
Raw materials, finished goods, and critical records shall be stored in designated protected locations.
The Company shall:

Monitor monthly water consumption.
Maintain water storage facilities.
Promote water conservation measures.
Evaluate opportunities for rainwater harvesting and water recycling.
The Company shall maintain backup power systems to support critical operations including:

Manufacturing equipment.
Laboratory operations.
Information technology systems.
Emergency lighting.
Fire protection systems.
Emergency generators shall be inspected and tested periodically.
9.6 Physical Hazard Control Measures
Fire Prevention and Protection. The Company shall maintain:

Fire detection systems.
Fire extinguishers.
Hydrant systems where applicable.
Emergency evacuation procedures.
Fire safety inspections shall be conducted periodically.
Chemical Spill Preparedness. The Company shall maintain:

Spill response kits.
Chemical handling procedures.
Emergency response instructions.
Appropriate personal protective equipment.
Employees involved in chemical handling shall receive appropriate training.
Equipment and Utility Failure Prevention. Critical equipment shall be covered under preventive maintenance programmes. Maintenance activities shall include:

Inspection.
Testing.
Calibration, where applicable.
Replacement of worn components.
Infrastructure Protection. Buildings, warehouses, utility areas, and storage facilities shall be inspected periodically to identify structural risks and maintenance requirements.
9.7 Business Continuity Planning. The Company shall maintain a documented Business Continuity Plan (BCP) covering critical operational activities. The BCP shall identify:

Critical business functions.
Key personnel and responsibilities.
Emergency communication channels.
Utility recovery arrangements.
Alternative operating arrangements.
Recovery priorities.
Each department shall identify activities essential for maintaining business operations during disruptions.
9.8 Supply Chain Continuity. The Procurement Department shall annually assess risks associated with critical suppliers and service providers. The assessment shall consider:

Geographic location.
Climate-related risks.
Transportation risks.
Dependency on single-source suppliers.
Historical supply disruptions.
Where feasible, alternate suppliers shall be identified for critical raw materials and services.
9.9 Information Technology and Data Continuity. The IT Department shall maintain measures to protect critical business information. Controls shall include:

Daily data backup.
Secure backup storage.
Controlled access to information systems.
Cybersecurity protection measures.
Periodic testing of data recovery capabilities.
Critical operational, quality, regulatory, and business records shall be protected from loss or unauthorized access.
9.10 Emergency Response and Recovery. Following a climate event, physical hazard incident, or significant disruption:
Initial Response

Ensure employee safety.
Secure affected areas.
Activate emergency response procedures.
Notify relevant management personnel.
Impact Assessment. Responsible departments shall assess:

Employee impacts.
Facility damage.
Equipment damage.
Utility disruptions.
Inventory losses.
Supply chain impacts.
Recovery Activities. The Company shall prioritize restoration of:

Employee safety systems.
Utilities.
Information systems.
Manufacturing operations.
Customer commitments.
Corrective actions shall be implemented to prevent recurrence where applicable.

blocks.text: Relevant employees shall receive training on:

Climate-related risks.
Emergency response procedures.
Fire safety.
Spill response.
Business continuity responsibilities.
Evacuation procedures.
Emergency drills may be conducted at least annually.

narrative.text: The Company shall monitor:

Climate risk assessments completed.
Physical hazard assessments completed.
Emergency drills conducted.
Business continuity tests performed.
Climate-related disruptions.
Utility interruptions.
Corrective actions implemented.
Results shall be reviewed by Senior Management annually.

sops.title: Confidential Information, Data Protection and Stakeholder Consent Procedure

blocks.text:
This procedure establishes the requirements for the collection, processing, storage, access, sharing, retention, and disposal of confidential information and personal data at Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

The objective is to protect employee, customer, supplier, contractor, and business information from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, loss, theft, or misuse while ensuring that personal information is collected and processed only for legitimate business purposes and with appropriate stakeholder consent where required.

This procedure applies to all employees, contract workers, consultants, suppliers, service providers, customers, visitors, and other stakeholders whose information is collected, processed, stored, or maintained by Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

The procedure applies to:

Employee records.
Recruitment and applicant information.
Customer information.
Supplier and contractor information.
Business contracts and agreements.
Financial and commercial records.
Electronic databases and software systems.
Emails and electronic communications.
Physical documents and records.

responsibilities: Provide oversight for information security and data protection practices.
Review significant data protection risks and incidents.
Ensure adequate resources are available for implementation of this procedure.
Maintain information security controls.
Manage user access rights.
Protect electronic information and databases.
Conduct periodic system backups.
Monitor cybersecurity risks.
Maintain confidentiality of employee and applicant records.
Obtain employee consent where required.
Restrict access to personnel records.
Ensure confidential information is used only for legitimate business purposes.
Approve access to sensitive information where applicable.
Report data protection incidents.
Protect confidential information under their control.
Follow data protection requirements.
Report actual or suspected breaches immediately.

body.text:
The Company shall collect only information necessary for operational, employment, legal, contractual, regulatory, quality, safety, or business purposes.

Information may be collected through:

Employment applications.
Vendor registration forms.
Customer agreements.
Contracts and purchase orders.
Regulatory submissions.
Business correspondence.
Personal information shall not be collected beyond legitimate business requirements.

Consent shall be obtained where required before collecting, processing, storing, or sharing personal information.

Consent may be obtained through:

Employment application forms.
Appointment letters and employment contracts.
Supplier registration forms.
Service agreements.
Customer agreements.
Written declarations and consent forms.
Electronic acceptance records.
Stakeholders shall be informed regarding:

Purpose of information collection.
Intended use of information.
Information sharing requirements, where applicable.
Record retention practices.

Access to confidential information shall be granted only to authorized personnel based on job responsibilities and business requirements.

Control measures may include:

Password-protected systems.
User access permissions.
Locked storage cabinets.
Controller server access.
Restricted document access.
Access rights shall be reviewed periodically and revoked when employees leave the organization or change roles.
Electronic information shall be protected through appropriate information security controls including:

Password protection.
Multi-user access controls.
Antivirus and malware protection.
Firewall protection.
Secure data storage.
Regular software updates.
Data backup procedures.
Critical business systems shall be accessible only to authorized users.

Confidential physical records shall be stored in secured locations with controlled access.

Examples include:

Employee files.
Payroll records.
Customer records.
Supplier records.
Regulatory documents.
Contracts and agreements.
Unauthorized copying, removal, or disclosure of confidential records is prohibited.

Employees, contractors, consultants, and third parties with access to confidential information shall maintain confidentiality during and after their engagement with the Company.

Confidential information shall not be:

Shared with unauthorized individuals.
Used for personal benefit.
Disclosed outside the organization without approval.
Distributed through unauthorized channels.
Confidentiality obligations may be supported through Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) or contractual confidentiality clauses.
Confidential or personal information shall only be disclosed:

For legitimate business purposes.
Under legal or regulatory requirements.
Under contractual obligations.
With stakeholder consent where applicable.
Before sharing information with external parties, the responsible department shall ensure appropriate confidentiality safeguards are in place.
Information shall be retained according to:

Legal requirements.
Regulatory obligations.
Contractual requirements.
Business needs.
When records are no longer required, disposal shall be performed securely through:

Shredding of physical documents.
Permanent deletion of electronic files.
Secure destruction methods approved by the Company.

Any actual or suspected data breach shall be reported immediately to the Department Head, HR Department, IT Department, or Management.

The investigation shall evaluate:

Nature of the breach.
Information affected.
Root cause.
Potential business impact.
Corrective actions required.
Appropriate containment, corrective, and preventive actions shall be implemented to reduce the risk of recurrence.
Employees handling confidential information shall receive periodic awareness training on:

Data protection requirements.
Confidentiality obligations.
Information security practices.
Cybersecurity awareness.
Data breach reporting procedures.
Training records shall be maintained by the relevant department.

narrative.text: The effectiveness of this procedure may be monitored through:

Number of data protection incidents reported.
Number of information security incidents.
Completion of data protection training.
Access control reviews completed.
Data breach investigations closed.
Compliance with confidentiality requirements.
Significant incidents shall be reported to Senior Management for review and corrective action.

sops.title: Cyber Incident Response and Business Recovery Procedure

blocks.text:
This procedure establishes a structured approach for identifying, reporting, assessing, responding to, containing, investigating, recovering from, and preventing information security incidents that may impact the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of company information, systems, applications, networks, and business operations.

The procedure aims to minimize operational disruption, protect confidential information, support business continuity, and strengthen the Company's cybersecurity resilience.
This procedure applies to:

All employees, contractors, consultants, and temporary personnel.
Information systems and applications.
Company-owned computers, laptops, servers, mobile devices, and storage media.
Email and communication platforms.
Cloud-based services and databases.
Network infrastructure.
Third-party systems connected to Company networks.

responsibilities: Monitor information security incidents.
Coordinate incident response activities.
Investigate security events.
Implement containment and recovery actions.
Maintain incident records.
Immediately report suspected security incidents.
Follow information security requirements.
Cooperate with investigations.
Support incident investigations.
Ensure affected employees follow recovery requirements.
Escalate significant incidents to Management.
Review significant incidents.
Approve major recovery actions where required.
Support implementation of corrective actions.

body.text: Information security incidents may be identified through:

Employee reports.
Security monitoring tools.
Antivirus alerts.
Network monitoring systems.
System access logs.
Third-party notifications.
Examples include:

Phishing emails.
Malware infections.
Ransomware attacks.
Unauthorized access attempts.
Loss of devices containing company information.
Data leakage incidents.
System compromise.
Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information.
All suspected incidents shall be reported to the IT Department immediately upon discovery.
The IT Department shall evaluate:

Type of incident.
Systems affected.
Information affected.
Potential business impact.
Regulatory implications.
Recovery requirements.
Incidents may be classified as:

rows: Significant business disruption, ransomware, major data breach
Malware infection or localized system compromise
Minor security violation with limited impact

body.text:
The IT Department shall take immediate action to limit the impact of the incident.

Containment measures may include:

Disconnecting affected devices.
Blocking malicious network activity.
Disabling compromised accounts.
Restricting unauthorized access.
Isolating affected systems.
The IT Department shall investigate:

Source of the incident.
Method of compromise.
Systems and information affected.
Duration of exposure.
Business impact.
Root cause analysis shall be documented for significant incidents.

Following containment and investigation, recovery activities shall be initiated.

Actions may include:

Restoration of systems from backups.
Reinstallation of software.
Recovery of business data.
Validation of system functionality.
Restoration of network connectivity.
Security testing prior to returning systems to operation.
Critical business systems shall be prioritized during recovery.
An incident may be closed after:

Recovery activities are completed.
Corrective actions are implemented.
Systems are verified as operational.
Incident documentation is completed.
Approval for closure shall be provided by the IT Manager or designated authority.

blocks.text: To support recovery activities:

Critical business data shall be backed up regularly.
Backup records shall be maintained securely.
Recovery testing shall be conducted periodically.
Access to backup systems shall be restricted.
Where security incidents impact business operations, applicable Business Continuity Plans shall be activated.
Following incident closure, corrective actions may include:

Security patch implementation.
Password resets.
Access control improvements.
Infrastructure upgrades.
Additional employee training.
Policy revisions.
Enhanced monitoring controls.
Actions shall be tracked to completion.
Employees shall receive periodic awareness training on:

Phishing prevention.
Password security.
Safe use of information systems.
Data protection requirements.
Incident reporting procedures.

narrative.text: The Company may monitor:

Number of information security incidents.
Data breach incidents.
Phishing reports.
Malware incidents.
Incident response times.
Recovery completion times.
Corrective actions completed.
Significant incidents shall be reviewed by Senior Management.

sops.title: Authorization and Approval Matrix for Financial, Procurement and Business Transactions Procedure

blocks.text: This procedure establishes a structured authorization and approval framework for financial, procurement, contractual, operational, and administrative transactions undertaken by Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.

The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that all transactions are properly reviewed, approved by authorized personnel, supported by appropriate documentation, aligned with approved budgets, and executed in accordance with the Company's internal control requirements.
The procedure also aims to prevent unauthorized commitments, financial irregularities, conflicts of interest, fraud, and approval bypasses.
This procedure applies to all departments and employees involved in initiating, reviewing, approving, processing, recording, or monitoring transactions, including:

Purchase requisitions
Purchase orders
Vendor onboarding
Capital expenditure (CAPEX)
Operational expenditure (OPEX)
Service contracts and agreements
Consultancy engagements
Employee reimbursements
Vendor payments
Asset purchases and disposals
Donations and sponsorships
Business commitments involving financial obligations

responsibilities: Approve high-value transactions and strategic commitments.
Approve major contracts and capital investments.
Review exceptional transactions exceeding approval limits.
Verify budget availability.
Review financial implications.
Process payments after approval verification.
Maintain transaction records.
Verify procurement approvals.
Conduct vendor due diligence.
Maintain supplier records and purchasing documentation.
Initiate and justify business requirements.
Review operational necessity.
Approve transactions within authorized limits.
Review adherence to authorization controls.
Identify approval violations and control weaknesses.

body.text: All transactions shall:

Have a valid business justification.
Be supported by appropriate documentation.
Be approved before execution.
Comply with approved budgets.
Be processed through authorized approval channels.
Be retained for audit and verification purposes.
No employee shall approve a transaction that directly benefits themselves or creates a conflict of interest.
Transactions exceeding approved budgets shall require additional approval from Management.
All procurement activities shall follow the approved procurement process.
Purchase Requisition
The requesting department shall submit a Purchase Requisition containing:

Description of item or service.
Quantity required.
Business justification.
Estimated value.
Required delivery date.
Procurement Approval Matrix
Approved Purchase Orders shall be issued before procurement activities commence.
Before onboarding a vendor, the following documents shall be verified:

GST Registration Certificate.
PAN Card.
Bank Account Details.
Company Registration Certificate.
MSME Certificate (where applicable).
Cancelled Cheque.
Business Licenses and Permits.

Vendor creation shall require review by Procurement and Finance Departments.

High-risk vendors may require additional management approval.

Only approved vendors shall be used for procurement activities.

All contracts shall be reviewed prior to execution.

The review shall consider:

Scope of work.
Commercial terms.
Payment conditions.
Compliance obligations.
Confidentiality requirements.
Legal and regulatory implications.
Contract Approval Matrix
Only authorized signatories may sign contracts on behalf of the Company.
All payments shall be supported by:

Approved Purchase Order.
Vendor Invoice.
Goods Receipt Note (GRN) or Service Completion Confirmation.
Payment Approval Form.
Payment Approval Matrix
Payments shall not be processed without supporting documentation.
Employees seeking reimbursement shall submit:

Expense Claim Form.
Original receipts or invoices.
Supporting approvals.
Reimbursement Approval Matrix
Incomplete claims may be rejected.
CAPEX proposals shall include:

Business justification.
Technical specifications.
Cost estimate.
Vendor quotation(s).
Expected business benefits.
CAPEX Approval Matrix
No capital asset purchase shall be initiated without approved CAPEX authorization.

blocks.text: All donations and sponsorships shall:

Be lawful and transparent.
Have a legitimate business or social purpose.
Be supported by documentation.
Receive management approval before commitment.
Political contributions shall not be made unless specifically permitted by applicable law and approved by the Managing Director.
To strengthen internal controls:

Requestor and approver shall be different individuals.
Procurement and payment functions shall be segregated.
Vendor creation and payment approval shall not be performed by the same employee.
Financial system access shall be restricted to authorized personnel.
Any exceptions shall be documented and approved by Management.

narrative.text: Compliance with this procedure shall be monitored through:

Internal audits.
Financial reviews.
Procurement reviews.
Payment verification checks.
Vendor management reviews.
Significant control violations shall be reported to Senior Management.

blocks.text: Failure to comply with this procedure may result in:

Transaction rejection.
Corrective action.
Disciplinary action.
Investigation of potential misconduct.
Unauthorized commitments made without approval may be considered a violation of Company policy.

This procedure establishes a formal mechanism for employees, contract workers, suppliers, contractors, customers, local communities, and other stakeholders to raise grievances, concerns, or complaints regarding labour practices, human rights, workplace conditions, ethics, environmental issues, health and safety matters, corruption, discrimination, harassment, or violations of company policies.

The procedure also establishes a structured remediation process to investigate confirmed concerns, implement corrective actions, address adverse impacts on affected stakeholders, and prevent recurrence.
This procedure applies to:

Permanent employees.
Contract workers and temporary workers.
Apprentices and trainees.
Suppliers and contractors.
Service providers.
Customers.
Local communities.
Other stakeholders interacting with Tagoor Laboratories Pvt Ltd.
The procedure covers concerns relating to:

Human rights and labour practices.
Harassment and discrimination.
Wage and benefit issues.
Working conditions and working hours.
Occupational health and safety.
Environmental impacts.
Ethical misconduct.
Corruption and bribery.
Supplier non-compliance.
Violations of company policies and applicable legal requirements.

responsibilities: Receive and register grievances.
Maintain grievance records.
Coordinate investigations.
Monitor closure of corrective actions and remediation plans.
Support investigations.
Provide relevant information and records.
Implement agreed corrective actions.
Investigate health, safety, and environmental concerns.
Verify implementation of corrective actions.
Review significant grievances.
Approve remediation plans where necessary.
Monitor closure of critical issues.
Raise concerns in good faith.
Cooperate with investigations.
Provide accurate information where available.

narrative.text: Grievances may be submitted through:

Reporting to Manager, Supervisor, Department Head or Human Resources Manager.
Email: hr@tagoorlab.com
Written Complaint submitted to the Human Resources Department.
Suggestion / Complaint Box located at the facility.
Senior Management
The Company shall maintain confidentiality and protect complainants from retaliation to the extent practicable.

body.text: Stakeholders may submit grievances verbally, in writing, via email, complaint boxes, or through designated reporting channels.
Anonymous grievances may also be accepted where sufficient information is available to conduct a review.
Upon receipt:

The grievance shall be entered into the Grievance Register.
A unique grievance reference number shall be assigned.
The date, source, and nature of the grievance shall be recorded.
Acknowledgement shall normally be provided within 7 working days where contact details are available.
The grievance shall be assessed to determine:

Nature of the issue.
Severity and urgency.
Stakeholders affected.
Potential legal, ethical, environmental, health and safety, or human rights implications.
High-risk grievances involving child labour, forced labour, harassment, discrimination, corruption, environmental incidents, or serious safety concerns shall be escalated immediately to Management.
The Company shall investigate grievances through:

Interviews with relevant personnel.
Review of records and documents.
Site inspections where necessary.
Collection of supporting evidence.
Investigations shall be conducted fairly, objectively, and confidentially.
Investigation findings shall be documented and classified as:

Substantiated.
Partially Substantiated.
Unsubstantiated.
Where allegations are substantiated or partially substantiated, the matter shall proceed to the Remediation Process.
The complainant shall be informed of the outcome where appropriate and permitted by confidentiality requirements.
The grievance shall be formally closed after completion of the investigation and documentation of findings.
A remediation process shall be initiated when investigations, audits, inspections, assessments, or monitoring activities confirm:

Human rights violations.
Labour rights violations.
Workplace harassment or discrimination.
Wage or benefit non-compliance.
Health and safety deficiencies.
Environmental incidents.
Ethical misconduct.
Supplier non-compliance.
Regulatory non-compliance.

steps.heading: 13.6.2 Impact Assessment and Root Cause Analysis

body.text: The responsible department shall evaluate:

The nature and severity of the issue.
Stakeholders affected.
Potential legal and regulatory implications.
Business impacts.
Root causes contributing to the issue.
Risk of recurrence.
A documented Remediation Action Plan shall be developed which includes:

Description of the issue.
Root cause identified.
Corrective actions required.
Remediation measures.
Responsible person(s).
Target completion dates.
Verification requirements.
Remediation actions may include:

rows: Payment of wage shortfall and payroll correction
Revision of work schedules and workforce planning
Investigation, disciplinary action, counselling, awareness training
Immediate removal from work, protection of the child, support for continued education
Immediate cessation of practice and worker protection measures
Containment, clean-up, corrective action and restoration
Supplier Corrective Action Plan and follow-up verification
Investigation, disciplinary action, and control strengthening

body.text: The responsible department shall verify that:

Corrective actions have been completed.
Remediation commitments have been fulfilled.
Supporting evidence is available.
The issue has been adequately addressed.
An effectiveness review shall be conducted to determine whether:

Root causes have been eliminated.
Similar incidents are unlikely to recur.
Additional actions are required.
The remediation case shall be formally closed after:

Completion of corrective actions.
Verification of effectiveness.
Approval by the responsible department or Management.
Closure records shall be retained for future review and audit purposes.

blocks.text: The Company prohibits retaliation against any person who reports a concern or participates in an investigation in good faith.
Retaliation may include:

Dismissal or termination.
Demotion.
Harassment.
Intimidation.
Discrimination.
Reduction of benefits or opportunities.
Any retaliation complaint shall be investigated separately and may result in disciplinary action.

narrative.text: The Company shall monitor:

Number of grievances received.
Number of grievances resolved.
Average grievance closure time.
Human rights-related grievances.
Health and safety grievances.
Ethics and compliance concerns.
Corrective actions completed within agreed timelines.
Repeat grievance trends.
Significant grievances and remediation actions shall be periodically reviewed by Management.
